correctness.rationale: For all n≥3, one transposition and two oriented 3-cycles exhaust the near-identity strata. Counting by span proves the two explicit rows and exact determinant 2r(r+1)-n. An analytic negative witness applies for every n≥5; full integer enumeration covers every 2×2 minor for n≤4. Conditional exchangeability of record positions given an individual fixed point proves the exact positive covariance for all n≥2. The standalone script passed 31,317 independent arithmetic assertions; finite enumeration is not used as an all-n proof.

value.rationale: This sharply classifies whether a natural strong-positive-dependence principle survives conditioning in permutations. Near-identity fixed-point layers are forced by transposition and three-cycle structures, yielding a complete all-size sign boundary, minimal failure at n=5, and a genuine disparity from the distinct cycle/fixed-point TP2 law despite record/cycle marginal equidistribution. Positive covariance alone would conceal the failure; the signed-minor exactness has structural and inferential value.
